# The Harmonic Method

> The specification and agent skills for the Harmonic Method — a single
> method for improving systems with explicit intent, preserved context, and
> decision lineage, applied here at system altitude. Coda, Beat, Beat Version,
> Revision, and Note are the same primitives at beat/track and portfolio
> altitude too — altitude is recursion, not a separate framework. Open to
> practice with any tools; Harmonica (harmonica.io), by Codazen, is the
> reference implementation.
> Full documentation: https://harmonicmethods.com

## Specs
- specs/coda.yml: Coda — the strategic outcome an entity exists to serve
- specs/beat.yml: Beat — a durable capability or process, laddering to a Coda
- specs/beat-version.yml: Beat Version — a planned step in a Beat's evolution
- specs/revision.yml: Revision — a tracked change executing part of a Beat Version.
  The relationship runs one way: a Revision belongs to exactly one Beat Version, and a
  Beat Version is delivered by one or more Revisions. Nothing bounds how many.
- specs/note.yml: Note — typed knowledge (background, constraint, guidance, decision)
- specs/conformance.yml: Conformance — which contents bind an implementation, which of those a tool can compare, and the declaration an implementation writes. Extensions conform; contradictions do not. A claim is made against a spec set version, never against the trunk.
- specs/spec-set.yml: the one version of the normative surface; every spec repeats it as a parsed spec_version field and the checker enforces agreement. Pin this number, not the repository tag — package.json versions the checker separately.
- specs/bar.yml: Bar — the recurring cadence period work is planned and delivered within; nests temporally via an optional parent, so a longer cadence is a Bar with children rather than a second entity
- specs/downbeat.yml: Downbeat — an immutable anchor recording where a capability stood and what it was converging toward; sits at beat altitude, so one Bar boundary yields one Downbeat per capability in view
- specs/function.yml: Function — the five accountabilities (Composer, Orchestrator, Conductor, Producer, Promoter); a concept, not an instantiable entity, and not a field on any entity

## Instruments
Each serves one of the five functions. A digest over each one's normative text
guards it against an unacknowledged edit.
- skills/beat-coda-quality-check/SKILL.md: Composer — score a Beat 1-5 across seven dimensions
- skills/beat-version-quality-check/SKILL.md: Orchestrator — score a Beat Version plan 1-5 across six dimensions
- skills/coda-alignment-check/SKILL.md: Conductor — reconcile a Coda chain across nine checks, reported as findings rather than a score
The Producer and Promoter have no instrument yet, deliberately.

## Producing
Two skills produce rather than assess. Neither carries dimensions or a scale,
neither is covered by the digest because there is nothing normative in either to
guard, and both defer every judgement they need to an instrument above by
pointing at the file.
- skills/beat-composing/SKILL.md: Composer — compose a Beat and its Coda from a
  plain description, ask for what is missing rather than inventing it, score the
  draft with beat-coda-quality-check read as written, then revise from that score
  and from the author's feedback
- skills/downbeat-taking/SKILL.md: Conductor — take an immutable anchor on one
  capability: the Coda frozen verbatim, and a reading of how far the work had
  converged toward it. Defines no scale, because downbeat.yml leaves computation
  to the implementation; separates what was examined from what was taken on the
  record's word; reports drift against the prior anchor or states that there is
  none to compare against

## Layout of a system
One rule all the way down: an entity is a directory, its children are
subdirectories. No file carries an inline child list — the directory is the
list. Notes attach to the Beat, never to a Beat Version, and may name the Beat
Version they arose from via the optional beat_version field.
- harmonic-method/coda.yml: the system Coda every Beat below ladders to
- harmonic-method/beats/<slug>/beat.yml: a durable capability
- harmonic-method/beats/<slug>/notes/: that Beat's typed knowledge
- harmonic-method/beats/<slug>/versions/<v>/version.yml: a planned step
- harmonic-method/beats/<slug>/versions/<v>/revisions/: the changes executing it — one or more

There is no checks/ directory by design: this repository assesses but does not record,
and no check entity is specified.

## This repository's own system
This repository described in its own vocabulary — real capabilities, real work in
flight, and the real decisions behind it, not illustrations.
- harmonic-method/: the Beats this repository delivers, their planned steps, and the
  Notes recording why each choice was made

## Worked example
- examples/: one conformant Beat, laid out exactly as harmonic-method/ is
- examples/declaration.yml: a worked conformance declaration, deliberately fictional
- examples/declaration-spec-kit.yml: the same form applied to GitHub's Spec Kit — a
  third-party reading, NOT a claim by its maintainers, who have declared nothing.
  The qualification is carried in the implementation field because that is what the
  checker prints. Do not cite it as a conformance result for that workflow.
